2026 DCF Research Scenario

 

The Borehole Is There—So Why Is Water Still a Problem?


Providing a borehole is only the beginning of ensuring reliable community water access. Keeping it functional requires maintenance, resources, and arrangements that meet the needs of the people who depend on it.


For this project, select a real community in Nigeria with an existing communal borehole that provides unreliable service. Choose a community you are familiar with or can credibly research through accessible sources. You do not need to live there or visit it.


Investigate the problem and propose a practical solution. Your research should establish the community’s actual circumstances; the funding and planning conditions below are hypothetical and apply to every candidate.


Your Assignment


Imagine that a donor has offered a one-time grant of ₦1,500,000 to improve the reliability of the selected community’s water service. Develop a 12-month plan showing how the grant would be used and how the improvements would be sustained afterward.


You are not expected to solve every water-access problem in the community. If the grant cannot fully resolve the issue, explain what meaningful improvement it can realistically achieve and what would remain unresolved.


Your proposal must address the following:


1.    Introduce the community and establish the problem: Name the community, LGA, and state. Describe the unreliable service, who is affected, and how they cope. Support your description with evidence.


2.    Investigate the causes: Research why the service may be unreliable. Distinguish supported findings from assumptions, and identify what needs checking before spending the grant.


3.    Learn from an existing example: Examine one real example of community water management. Explain what you would learn from it and adapt locally.


4.    Compare solutions and justify your choice: Compare two possible approaches and justify your choice. Explain what the grant can realistically achieve and what would remain unresolved.


5.    Develop a practical 12-month plan: Provide a simple budget and timeline within the ₦1,500,000 grant and 12-month period. Assign responsibility for operations, maintenance, water-quality checks, and transparent management of funds.


6.    Address affordability and continuity: Explain how running costs would be covered during and after the project, including support for households unable to pay. Justify any reliance on additional funding or volunteers.


7.    Respond to a hypothetical setback: After three months, recurring funding falls to half the amount expected. Explain your adjustments and what you would protect. If your plan needs no recurring funding, justify this and address an unexpected maintenance expense instead.


8.    Assess whether your solution works: Identify three measures of success, their starting points or how you would establish them, and your 12-month targets. State your plan’s biggest weakness and how you would manage it.


Research Expectations


This is a research project. Your submission should demonstrate that you have investigated the problem and used what you learned to develop your solution.


Use at least three relevant sources. These may include freely available reports, news

Prices updated August 2026 · Nigeria
Typical price ranges
Item | Typical cost | Notes |
Shallow borehole (60–100ft, soft terrain) | ₦800,000 – ₦1,600,000 | Common in parts of Lagos, Bayelsa and Delta. |
Deep borehole (150–300ft) | ₦2,000,000 – ₦4,500,000 | Required in Abuja, Jos, Enugu and most rocky terrain. |
Submersible pump + control panel | ₦350,000 – ₦1,200,000 | Sized by depth and head; solar-pump option adds ₦600k+. |
Overhead tank and stand | ₦450,000 – ₦1,800,000 | 1,000–5,000 litre tank on steel or block stand. |
Iron / hardness filtration skid | ₦300,000 – ₦1,500,000 | Sand, carbon and softener stages sized by flow rate. |
Reverse osmosis drinking unit | ₦180,000 – ₦900,000 | Under-sink to light commercial capacity. |
Water quality lab test | ₦25,000 – ₦80,000 | Do this before buying any treatment equipment. |
Ranges reflect quotes commonly seen on SustifyHomes across Nigerian states. Final pricing depends on site conditions and equipment availability.

Send this to verified providers How SustifyHomes escrow works
What changes the price
Geology and depth
Rocky terrain needs percussion or rotary rigs and more casing, which is the single biggest cost driver.
Water chemistry
High iron, hardness or salinity changes the treatment train entirely. Always test before specifying.
Daily demand
A household of six at 120 litres per person needs roughly 720 litres a day; commercial demand scales pumps, storage and filter size.
Power source
Solar pumping removes recurring diesel and grid cost but adds upfront panels, controller and sometimes a dedicated tank.
Frequently asked questions
How much does it cost to drill a borehole in Lagos? Shallow Lagos boreholes typically cost ₦800,000 – ₦1,600,000 in 2026. Deeper drilling into harder terrain, or sites needing extensive casing, moves toward ₦2m and above.
Do I need treatment if my borehole water looks clear? Yes — clear water can still carry dissolved iron, hardness and bacteria. A lab test costing ₦25,000 – ₦80,000 tells you exactly which stages you need.
How long does a borehole take to complete? Drilling usually takes one to three days; pump installation, tank and treatment add a further three to seven days.
How often should filters be serviced? Sediment and carbon media are typically replaced every 6–12 months, and RO membranes every two to three years depending on feed quality.

Posted in Cost Analysis Homes
Posted by
Folagbade Daniel
July 27, 2026 No Comments
Budget somewhere between ₦900,000 and ₦2,500,000 (~$580–$1,610) for a complete borehole and water system in Nigeria in 2026 — that’s the all-in figure for a standard home. That splits into drilling (₦600,000–₦1,600,000 depending on depth), the pump and installation (₦300,000–₦900,000), and a separate overhead tank and stand (₦300,000–₦900,000+). Lagos sits at the top of the range — ₦800,000–₦2,500,000 — because of hard ground and high demand. A basic manual (hand-dug) borehole can start around ₦120,000–₦500,000 but delivers less reliable water. Prices are at ₦1,550/$, July 2026.
Here’s a cost that ambushes almost every self-builder in Nigeria. You budget carefully for blocks, cement, roofing — and then remember the house needs water, and there’s no reliable public supply to connect to. So you’re drilling your own borehole. The question is: what does that actually cost in 2026? Let’s break it down honestly, including the parts most quotes quietly leave out.
How much does a borehole cost in Nigeria in 2026?
For a standard residential borehole with a good pump and storage, budget ₦900,000 to ₦2,500,000 all-in. The spread is wide because three things move the price hard: how deep you have to drill, the ground you’re drilling through, and where in the country you are. A shallow borehole in soft soil up-country is a different job from a deep one through Lagos rock.
Component | Typical 2026 cost (₦) | ~$ (₦1,550/$) |
Drilling (by depth/soil) | 600,000–1,600,000 | 385–1,030 |
Submersible pump + installation | 300,000–900,000 | 195–580 |
Overhead tank + stand/base | 300,000–900,000+ | 195–580+ |
Plumbing, wiring & connection to house | 150,000–400,000 | 95–260 |
Water treatment / filtration (if needed) | 100,000–500,000+ | 65–320+ |
Typical all-in (standard home) | 900,000–2,500,000 | 580–1,610 |
Why Lagos costs more
Lagos is one of the most expensive places in Nigeria to drill, with typical jobs landing between ₦800,000 and ₦2,500,000 . Two reasons: the ground in much of the state is hard and demands heavier rigs, and demand is so high that good drillers charge accordingly. In swampy or coastal areas (parts of Lekki, Ajah, the island fringes) you may also need deeper drilling and better casing to reach clean water and keep salt out — which pushes you toward the top of the range.
Worth knowing: Depth is the single biggest cost driver. A 60–100m borehole is far cheaper than a 150–250m one. Before you build, ask neighbours or local drillers how deep the water table is in that specific area — it can swing your quote by a million naira.
Manual vs mechanised: what you’re really choosing
A manually drilled (hand-dug) borehole can start as low as ₦120,000–₦500,000, and for a tight budget in soft-soil areas it can work. But be clear on the trade-off: manual boreholes are shallower, more prone to running dry in harmattan, and more likely to draw contaminated surface water. A mechani

How Much Does It Cost To Dig Borehole in Nigeria
Nigeria is still suffering a worrying problem of shortage water supply.
Different government water schemes in Nigeria seems to have been unsustainable and many has failed.
This leaves many citizens with the choice of getting water through private means.
In Nigeria, borehole is one of the most popular ways of water supply and storage.
Borehole drilling and digging cost in Nigeria,though expensive,is the best form of steady water supply in Nigeria.
However, borehole drilling cost in Nigeria is highly expensive.
So, this write up will center on borehole drilling & digging costs in Nigeria.
Borehole drilling has became the only sustainable means by which individuals and citizen access water interrupted all through the year and season.
However, the cost and price of borehole drilling in Nigeria is high and relative.
In otherwords, only very few citizens and individuals in Nigeria can afford to drill and install borehole water in Nigeria.
This still leaves many Nigerians without uninterrupted source of water supply. Nevertheless, borehole drilling is very rampant and popular in Nigeria.
It gives users access to water at all times. But the big question is at what cost can someone dig or drill a borehole in Nigeria.
This is the major focus of this post. The price of digging or drilling borehole in Nigeria will be talked about extensively in this article.
If you are also seeking for the cost of sinking borehole in Nigeria, Lagos, Port Harcourt or Anambra, this post will be your guide.
Cost of Borehole Drilling in Nigeria
How Much it costs to drill or sink borehole across Nigeria is not same price.
The cost and price for drilling borehole water in Nigeria is relative and most times based on topography of the areas in question.
The price of drilling borehole in some parts of Nigeria is way cheaper because of the nature of the areas.
Cost of borehole drilling is likely to be cheaper in a riverine areas unlike in desert areas.
These are some of the factors that plays on the price and cost of drilling borehole in Nigeria.
However, on average, the cost of drilling borehole in Nigeria is between N200,000 to N600,000 excluding construction of overhead tanks and tanks.
This average price of digging borehole might be higher in some places that has high desertification.
In this article,you will discover the average cost price of installation,drilling and sinking of borehole water in Nigeria.
Cost of Drilling Borehole in Northern Nigeria
It Cost a fortune to drill and install borehole in northern Nigeria.
This is because of the desertication that is witnessed across most Nigerian northern states.
However, there are some northern states that water can be accessed easily and they cost cheaper.
The price and cost of borehole drilling in Abuja, Adamawa, Kaduna, Kano, Plateau, Kwara, Kogi and Niger states is between N450,000 to N600,000.
